document.abstract: MOST of the owners of theatres and the engineers who design heating and ventilating plants for theatres have largely failed to consider the wide difference in the requirements of a standard theatre and moving picture theatre. There is hardly any more resemblance in their respective requirements than there is in the provisions to be made to ventilate a school house or a church, yet it has been the general practice to apply the same proportions and employ about the same standards of apparatus for both types of theatre buildings.
